questions.knowledge_point: Solving a Trigonometric Equation Involving Sine Under a Modified Domain
questions.problem: Calculate, in degrees, rounded to the nearest integer, the solutions to the equation $9\operatorname{sin}⁡x=-8$ for $-{180}^{∘}<x\le {180}^{∘}.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we rearrange the equation, isolating $\operatorname{sin}⁡x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}9\operatorname{sin}⁡x & =-8 \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡x & =-\frac{8}{9}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we find the principal value:

$$
\begin{aligned}x=\operatorname{arcsin}⁡(-\frac{8}{9})=-62.733\,955{…}^{∘}≈-{62.73}^{∘}\end{aligned}
$$

Since $-{62.73}^{∘}$ lies inside the range, our first solution is ${x}_{1}=-{62.73}^{∘}.$

Our first solution lies in the fourth quadrant and has a reference angle of ${\theta }_{R}={62.73}^{∘}.$ Since $\operatorname{sin}⁡x<0,$ the second solution must lie in the third quadrant, and it also has a reference angle ${\theta }_{R}={62.73}^{∘}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13992768/assets/62808ce876d31757e1b46863b014bbf83209c414099ade0f93b91303c6702d1f.png)

A second solution $X$ lies in the $3$rd quadrant, and we can find it using the reference angle as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}X & ={180}^{∘}+{\theta }_{R} \\  & ={180}^{∘}+{62.73}^{∘} \\  & ={242.73}^{∘}\end{aligned}
$$

However, this value is not in the required domain. To get the second solution ${x}_{2}$ that's within the given domain, we simply subtract ${360}^{∘}:$

$$
{x}_{2}=X-{360}^{∘}={242.73}^{∘}-{360}^{∘}=-{117.27}^{∘}
$$

So, the solutions (rounded to the nearest integer) are $x=-{117}^{∘},-{63}^{∘}.$

questions.knowledge_point: Solving a Trigonometric Equation Involving Sine with Quadrantal Angles
questions.worked_solution:
First, we rearrange the equation, isolating $\operatorname{sin}⁡x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}5\operatorname{sin}⁡x+5 & =0 \\ 5\operatorname{sin}⁡x & =-5 \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡x & =-1\end{aligned}
$$

 

Now, we find the principal value:

$$
x=\operatorname{arcsin}⁡(-1)=-\frac{\pi }{2}
$$

Since $-\frac{\pi }{2}$ lies inside the required domain, our first solution is ${x}_{1}=-\frac{\pi }{2}.$ 

As this is a quadrantal angle, to find the remaining solutions, we use our knowledge of the sine function. We know that the sine function has its minimum values at:

$$
x=-\frac{\pi }{2}+2n\pi 
$$

Since the domain $-\pi <x\le \pi $ is one period, and we have already found one minimum value in this period, we conclude that $x=-\frac{\pi }{2}$ is the only solution.

Since ${58.2117}^{∘}$ lies inside the given domain, our first solution is ${x}_{1}={58.2117}^{∘}.$

Our first solution lies in the first quadrant and has a reference angle of ${\theta }_{R}={58.2117}^{∘}.$ Since $\operatorname{sin}⁡x>0,$ the second solution must lie in the second quadrant, and it also has a reference angle ${\theta }_{R}={58.2117}^{∘}.$

questions.problem:
Expressed in **ascending order** in radians, rounded to one decimal place, the solutions to the equation $\operatorname{sin}⁡x=\frac{3}{5},$ for $-\pi <x\le \pi ,$  are

$x≈$
{{field-1}}$,\,x≈$

questions.worked_solution:
First, we find the principal value:

$$
\begin{aligned}x=\operatorname{arcsin}⁡(\frac{3}{5})=0.643\,501…≈0.6435\end{aligned}
$$

Since $0.6435$ lies inside the given domain, our first solution is ${x}_{1}=0.6435.$

Our first solution lies in the first quadrant and has a reference angle of ${\theta }_{R}=0.6435.$ Since $\operatorname{sin}⁡x>0,$ the second solution must lie in the second quadrant, and it also has a reference angle ${\theta }_{R}=0.6435.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13992768/assets/962545fd6fa64e121a99eb8bf684484e4b457dbd4defedd7c07ae88fd47cac6e.png)

Since the second solution ${x}_{2}$ lies in the $2$nd quadrant, we can find it using the reference angle as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} & =\pi -{\theta }_{R} \\  & =\pi -0.6435 \\  & ≈2.4981.\end{aligned}
$$

So, in ascending order, rounded to one decimal place, the solutions are 

$$
x≈0.6,\,x≈2.5.
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Solving a Trigonometric Equation Involving Sine with Quadrantal Angles
questions.worked_solution:
First, we rearrange the equation, isolating $\operatorname{sin}⁡x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}4\sqrt{3}\,\operatorname{sin}⁡x+4\sqrt{3} & =0 \\ 4\sqrt{3}\,\operatorname{sin}⁡x & =-4\sqrt{3} \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡x & =-1\end{aligned}
$$

 

Now, we find the principal value:

$$
x=\operatorname{arcsin}⁡(-1)=-\frac{\pi }{2}
$$

Since $-\frac{\pi }{2}$ does not lie inside the required domain $0\le x<2\pi ,$ we add one full period of $2\pi $ to find an equivalent angle in the domain:

$$
-\frac{\pi }{2}+2\pi =\frac{3\pi }{2}
$$

Thus, our first solution in the required domain is ${x}_{1}=\frac{3\pi }{2}.$ 

As this is a quadrantal angle, to find the remaining solutions, we use our knowledge of the sine function. We know that the sine function has its minimum values at:

$$
x=\frac{3\pi }{2}+2n\pi 
$$

Since the domain $0\le x<2\pi $ is one period, and we have already found one minimum value in this period, we conclude that $x=\frac{3\pi }{2}$ is the only solution.
